record.title: The optimal packing conjecture for nine congruent circles on a square flat torus
record.statement:
Let ${\mathbb T}^2$ be the square flat torus, and consider arrangements of 9 points representing the centers of 9 congruent circles. Let $d$ denote the maximal possible minimum distance between two points in the torus.

**Nine-point packing conjecture.** There is one unique, up to isometry, optimal arrangement of 9 points in ${\mathbb T}^2$, shown in the paper's Figure 9, with

$$
d=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{5+2\sqrt{3}}}\approx0.3437.
$$

This conjecture extends the paper's proved optimal-packing results for $N=6$, $7$, and $8$ and predicts both the exact optimal separation and uniqueness of the arrangement for $N=9$.
record.source_name: Oleg R. Musin and Anton V. Nikitenko, “Optimal packings of congruent circles on a square flat torus”, arXiv:1212.0649 (2012).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1212.0649

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2012).

record.title: Fujita–Nakamigawa conjecture on the balanced decomposition number
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a connected graph. Its **balanced decomposition number** is the minimum integer $s$ such that, for every balanced coloring $V(G)=P_1\uplus P_2\uplus X$ with $|P_1|=|P_2|$, there is a partition $V(G)=V_1\uplus\cdots\uplus V_r$ in which every induced subgraph $G[V_i]$ is connected, $|V_i\cap P_1|=|V_i\cap P_2|$, and $|V_i|\leq s$. A graph is **2-connected** if it has vertex-connectivity at least $2$.

**Fujita–Nakamigawa's conjecture.** If $G$ is $2$-connected, then its balanced decomposition number is at most

$$
\left\lfloor\frac{|V(G)|}{2}\right\rfloor+1.
$$

This conjecture connects the balanced decomposition number with vertex-connectivity and was motivated by pebble motion on graphs. It was announced as solved by G. J. Chang and N. Narayanan.
record.source_name: Tadashi Sakuma, “On the balanced decomposition number”, arXiv:1212.2308 (2014).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1212.2308

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of December 2012).

record.title: Symmetry conjecture for minimizers of the circulant analytic functional
record.statement:
Let $N=4n$, and let

$$
\Phi=\sum_{i+j+k+l=0}q_iq_jq_kq_l
$$

be minimized over vectors $q\in\mathbb T^N$ satisfying $\bar q_i=q_{-i}$. In the parametrization described immediately before the conjecture, write the corresponding vectors as having parameters $a$ and $c$. **Symmetry conjecture for minimizers.** The minimum over all such vectors is equal to the minimum over the vectors in this parametrized family satisfying $a=c$. The computations at $N=8$ and $N=12$ motivate this symmetry reduction, but the source does not establish it in general.
record.source_name: Teodor Banica, Ion Nechita and Jean-Marc Schlenker, “Analytic aspects of the circulant Hadamard conjecture”, arXiv:1212.3589 (2013).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1212.3589

Status: **open** according to the source (as of December 2012). “One open problem here is to decide whether $\min\Phi-N^2$ converges to $0$ or not, with $N\to\infty$.”

record.title: Chang–Narayanan conjecture on strong edge-colorings of degenerate graphs
record.statement:
A graph $G$ is **$k$-degenerate** if every subgraph of $G$ has minimum degree at most $k$. Let $G$ be a $k$-degenerate graph with maximum degree $Delta$, and let $c7_s'(G)$ denote its strong chromatic index.

**Chang–Narayanan conjecture.** There exists an absolute constant $c$ such that

$$
\chi_s'(G)\le ck^2\Delta.
$$

Furthermore, the factor $k^2$ may be replaced by $k$.

Chang and Narayanan proved the corresponding linear bound in $Delta$ for $2$-degenerate graphs with $c7_s'(G)\le 10\Delta-10$, and subsequent work improved this to $8\Delta-4$. The conjectured dependence on $k$, particularly the replacement of $k^2$ by $k$, remains open in the source context.
record.source_name: Gexin Yu, “Strong edge-colorings for k-degenerate graphs”, arXiv:1212.6093 (2013).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1212.6093

Status: **open** according to the source (as of December 2012).

record.title: Lucchini–Detomi's monolithicity conjecture for sigma-elementary groups
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a group with finite covering number 
$$
sigma(G)$, where
$$
sigma(G)$ is the smallest number of proper subgroups needed to cover $G$. Call $G$ **
$$
sigma$-elementary** if
$$
$sigma(G)<$sigma(G/N)
$$
for every non-trivial normal subgroup $N$ of $G$. A group is **monolithic** if it has a unique minimal normal subgroup. **Lucchini–Detomi's conjecture.** Every non-abelian
$$
sigma$-elementary group is monolithic. This conjecture concerns the structure of groups that are minimal, with respect to quotienting by non-trivial normal subgroups, among groups with a given covering number. The source gives no resolution, so the conjecture is recorded as open.
record.source_name: Martino Garonzi, “Covering monolithic groups with proper subgroups”, arXiv:1301.0743 (2013).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1301.0743

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2013).

record.title: Gao–Wang's conjecture on the maximal cross number of UFIMs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite abelian group. For an indexed multiset $S$ over $G\setminus\{0\}$, let $k(S)$ be the sum of $1/\operatorname{ord}(g)$ over its elements, and let $K_1(G)$ be the maximum of $k(S)$ over all unique factorization indexed multisets over $G\setminus\{0\}$. Writing $G$ as a direct sum of prime-power cyclic groups, define

$$
K_1^*(G):= \sum_{i=1}^n \sum_{j=1}^{n_i} \frac{p_i^{e_{ij}} - 1}{p_i^{e_{ij}}-p_i^{e_{ij}-1}}.
$$

**Gao–Wang's conjecture.** For every finite abelian group $G$,

$$
K_1(G)=K_1^*(G).
$$

This conjecture asks for an explicit formula for the maximal cross number of unique factorization indexed multisets and is presented as the main focus of the paper. Its resolution is stated to remain open.
record.source_name: Daniel Kriz, “On the maximal cross number of unique factorization indexed multisets”, arXiv:1301.1401 (2013).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1301.1401

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2013).

record.title: Bounded-dimensional orthostochasticity conjecture
record.statement:
Let ${\mathcal B}_n$ denote the set of bistochastic $n\times n$ matrices, and let $d_{\min}(n)$ be the smallest value of $d$ such that every matrix in ${\mathcal B}_n$ is $d$-orthostochastic. **Bounded-dimensional orthostochasticity conjecture.** There exists $n_0$ such that, for every $n\ge n_0$, 

$$
2\le d_{\min}(n)\le 3.
$$

This conjecture asserts that the number of real dimensions needed to represent all bistochastic matrices by orthostochastic constructions remains bounded as the matrix size grows. The surrounding discussion presents it as plausible based on the preceding results and dimensional considerations; its resolution is not given in the source.
record.source_name: Eugene Gutkin, “On a multi-dimesional generalization of the notion of orthostochastic and unistochastic matrices”, arXiv:1301.2537 (2013).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1301.2537

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2013).

record.title: Mubayi–Verstraëte conjecture on Turán numbers of linear cycles
record.statement:
Let $n$, $k$, and $\ell$ be integers with $n,k,\ell\geq 3$, and set $t=\left\lfloor\frac{\ell-1}{2}\right\rfloor$. Write ${\rm ex}_k(n,{\cal C}^{(k)}_\ell)$ for the maximum number of edges in a $k$-uniform hypergraph on $n$ vertices containing no linear cycle of length $\ell$.

**Mubayi–Verstraëte conjecture.** As $n\to\infty$,

$$
{\rm ex}_k(n,{\cal C}^{(k)}_\ell)=t\binom{n-1}{k-1}+O(n^{k-2}).
$$

This conjecture asserts that the natural lower bound for the Turán number of a linear cycle is asymptotically tight for all $k,\ell\geq 3$; the cited work had established matching bounds up to a constant factor in general, with stronger estimates in some cases.
record.source_name: Zoltan Furedi and Tao Jiang, “Hypergraph Turan numbers of linear cycles”, arXiv:1302.2387 (2013).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1302.2387

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2013).

record.title: Trapa's conjecture on connected components of symmetric clan orbits
record.statement:
Let $K$ be the relevant subgroup acting on the flag variety $G/B$, and let $Q_\gamma$ be the $K$-orbit corresponding to a symmetric $(2,n-2)$-clan $\gamma=(c_1,\ldots,c_n)$ in type $B$ or $D$. A clan is symmetric when reversing its characters gives the same clan: signs are preserved under reversal, and paired numbers are matched under reversal.

**Trapa's conjecture.** For both even and odd $n$, the orbit $Q_\gamma$ is disconnected if and only if, for every $i$ such that $c_i\in\mathbb{N}$, one has $c_i\neq c_{n+1-i}$.

This conjecture gives the combinatorial criterion needed to determine whether the relevant orbit has one or two components, and hence to describe the weak-order poset of the associated orbit space. The supplied text gives no resolution evidence.
record.source_name: Benjamin J. Wyser, “Some conjectures regarding certain Schubert structure constants in Lie types B and D”, arXiv:1302.3157 (2013).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1302.3157

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2013).

record.title: Conjecture on limit points of zeros of exponential-integral sections
record.statement:
Let $F$ be an exponential integral function as defined in the paper, and let $s_n[F](nz)$ denote its normalized sections. Let $D_{a,b}$ and $D_\text{imag}$ be the curves introduced in the paper as the candidate limit curves for the zeros of these sections. **Limit-curve conjecture.** All limit points of the zeros of $s_n[F](nz)$ lie on

$$
D_{a,b}\cup D_\text{imag}.
$$

The conjecture asserts that the exceptional countable set allowed by the paper's general theorem is always empty. Numerical examples studied by the author exhibit no limit points outside these curves, but a proof that this holds for every exponential integral function remains open.
record.source_name: Antonio R. Vargas, “Limit curves for zeros of sections of exponential integrals”, arXiv:1302.3695 (2014).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1302.3695

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2013).

record.title: Linear excess conjecture for the exact-colour spectrum
record.statement:
Let $\psi(k)$ denote the minimum possible size of $\mathcal{F}_{\Delta}$ over surjective $k$-colourings $\Delta:\mathbb{N}^{(2)}\twoheadrightarrow[k]$. **Linear excess conjecture.** There is an absolute constant $\epsilon>0$ such that

$$
\psi\left(\binom{n}{2}+3\right)>(1+\epsilon)n
$$

for all natural numbers $n\geq2$. The paper establishes nearby exact values and bounds for $\psi$, but explicitly states that this strengthening is not proved; determining $\psi$ completely remains open.
record.source_name: Bhargav Narayanan, “Exactly m-coloured complete infinite subgraphs”, arXiv:1303.2103 (2016).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1303.2103

Status: **open** according to the source (as of March 2013). “The problem of determining $\psi$ completely is of course still open.”

record.title: Nordhaus et al.'s conjecture on maximum and minimum genus
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph, with minimum genus $\gamma(G)$ and maximum genus $\Gamma(G)$. A graph is **upper-embeddable** if it has a one- or two-face embedding and hence satisfies $\Gamma(G)=\lfloor\beta(G)/2\rfloor$. **Nordhaus et al.'s conjecture.**

$$
\Gamma(G) \geq 2\gamma(G)
$$

for all graphs $G$. The conjecture concerns the relationship between maximum and minimum genus and is stronger than the corresponding general lower bound; the source later discusses counterexamples to the associated equality condition.
record.source_name: Timothy Sun, “On Milgram's construction and the Duke embedding conjectures”, arXiv:1303.2304 (2013).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1303.2304

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of March 2013). “With regards to Conjecture , all the known counterexamples are either graphs of large girth or scaffolded graphs, and they also violate Duke's conjecture.”

record.title: The two-fold sumset threshold conjecture for multiplicative subgroups
record.statement:
Let $p$ be a prime and let $A$ be a multiplicative subgroup of $\mathbb Z_p^*$. For a positive integer $k$, write $kA=\{x_1+\dots+x_k:x_i\in A,1\leq i\leq k\}$. **Two-fold sumset threshold conjecture.** If

$$
|A|>p^{\frac 12+\epsilon},\qquad \epsilon>0,
$$

then $2A$ contains $\mathbb Z_p^*$. The question concerns the smallest exponent forcing a two-fold sumset of a multiplicative subgroup to contain every nonzero residue; the paper's abstract establishes a related six-fold sumset result at exponent $\frac{11}{23}+\epsilon$, while the stated two-fold assertion is presented as an open question in the supplied text.
record.source_name: Derrick Hart, “A note on sumsets of subgroups in Z_p^*”, arXiv:1303.2729 (2013).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1303.2729

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2013).

record.title: The critical exponent conjecture for powers of doubly nonnegative matrices
record.statement:
Let $m(n)$ denote the smallest real number such that, for every $n$-by-$n$ doubly nonnegative matrix $A$, the conventional power $A^\alpha$ is doubly nonnegative for all $\alpha\geq m(n)$. The quantity $m(n)$ is called the critical exponent.

**Critical exponent conjecture.** For all integers $n\geq 2$, 

$$
m(n)=n-2.
$$

The conjecture extends the result known for $n<6$, while the general case remains open in the supplied source context.
record.source_name: Dominique Guillot, Apoorva Khare and Bala Rajaratnam, “The critical exponent conjecture for powers of doubly nonnegative matrices”, arXiv:1303.4701 (2013).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1303.4701

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2013).

record.title: Polynomial defining the maximal-dimensional augmentation component for knots
record.statement:
Let $K\subset\mathbb{R}^3$ be a knot, let $HC_*(K)$ be its contact homology algebra, and let

$$
V_K=\setn{(\epsilon(\lambda),\epsilon(\mu))}{\epsilon\text{ is an augmentation of }HC_*(K)}\subset(\mathbb{C}^*)^2.
$$

Let $\overline{V_K}$ denote the closure of $V_K$. **Polynomial-component conjecture.** The maximum-dimensional component of $\overline{V_K}$ is the vanishing set of a polynomial for every knot $K\subset\mathbb{R}^3$. This asserts algebraicity of the maximal-dimensional augmentation component, a property relevant to the relationship between knot contact homology and polynomial knot invariants. The supplied text gives no resolution or further scope for this claim.
record.source_name: Christopher Cornwell, “Knot contact homology and representations of knot groups”, arXiv:1303.4943 (2014).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1303.4943

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2013).

record.title: The Zarankiewicz number conjecture for orders three below a projective-plane order
record.statement:
Let $z(n)$ denote the maximum number of edges in a bipartite graph with partite sets of order $n$ that contains no cycle of length four. For a prime power $k$, consider the order $n=k^2+k-3$. **Zarankiewicz number conjecture.** For every prime power $k$, 

$$
z(k^2+k-3)=k^3+2k^2-6k+2.
$$

The conjecture extends the known values for $k=2,3,4$ and would give the expected general upper bound in the first case not covered by the preceding theorem. The authors state that they were unable to prove the bound for general prime powers, although the case $k=4$ is established separately.
record.source_name: Janusz Dybizbański, Tomasz Dzido and Stanisław Radziszowski, “On Some Zarankiewicz Numbers and Bipartite Ramsey Numbers for Quadrilateral”, arXiv:1303.5475 (2014).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1303.5475

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2013).

record.title: Fyodorov and Keating's short-interval maximum conjecture for the Riemann zeta function
record.statement:
Let $\zeta(s)$ denote the Riemann zeta function. For $T>0$, consider its maximum on the interval $[T,T+2\pi]$.

**Fyodorov and Keating's conjecture.** Let $\epsilon>0$. For $T_1$ sufficiently large depending on $\epsilon$, for all $T_1\leq T\leq 2T_1$, outside a set of “bad” values of $T$ of measure at most $\epsilon T_1$, one has

$$
\max_{T\leq t\leq T+2\pi}|\zeta(1/2+it)|=\exp(\log\log T-(3/4)\log\log\log T+O_{\epsilon}(1)),
$$

where $O_{\epsilon}(1)$ denotes a quantity bounded in terms of $\epsilon$. This refines the expected order of the maximum of $|\zeta(1/2+it)|$ over a short interval and is related to a more precise conjecture for the distribution of its logarithm; its status is not resolved here.
record.source_name: Adam J. Harper, “A note on the maximum of the Riemann zeta function, and log-correlated random variables”, arXiv:1304.0677 (2013).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1304.0677

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2013).

record.title: The generic nonsymmetric matrix equation conjecture for cubic systems
record.statement:
Let $K$ be the base field, let $n=3$, and let $B,C,D$ be generic $3\times 3$ matrices. Consider Eq., the nonsymmetric generic matrix equation in the unknown matrix $X\in\mathcal{M}_3(\overline{K})$. The **generic cubic system conjecture.** The solution count and Galois group of Eq. are

$$
(56,S_{56}).
$$

For $n=3$, numerical specializations over $\mathbb{Q}$ exhibit a degree-$56$ polynomial with Galois group $S_{56}$, motivating this conjecture; the asserted generic result is not established in the supplied text.
record.source_name: Gerald Bourgeois, “Nonsymmetric generic matrix equations”, arXiv:1304.2506 (2015).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1304.2506

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2013).

record.title: Weak $K_9$-minor-free graph structural conjecture
record.statement:
Let $\delta(G)$ denote the minimum degree of $G$, and let a graph be **$K_9$-minor free** if it has no $K_9$ minor. **Weak $K_9$ structural conjecture.** Any $K_9$-minor-free graph $G$ with

$$
\delta(G)=13
$$

has an edge $uv$ such that $u$ has degree $13$ and $uv$ belongs to at most $6$ triangles. The source presents this as an open structural statement that would imply a $12$-colorability result for $K_9$-minor-free graphs.
record.source_name: Boris Albar and Daniel Gonçalves, “On triangles in K_r-minor free graphs”, arXiv:1304.5468 (2013).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1304.5468

Status: **open** according to the source (as of April 2013). “This conjecture has been proved for $k \leq 5$ but remains open for $k \geq 6$.”

record.title: Large matching minimum degree conjecture for uniform hypergraphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a $k$-uniform hypergraph on $n$ vertices. For integers $n$, $d$, $k$, and $s$ with $1\leq d\leq k-1$ and $0\leq s\leq (1-\varepsilon)n/k$, let $m_d^s(k,n)$ denote the minimum integer $m$ such that every $k$-uniform hypergraph on $n$ vertices with minimum $d$-degree at least $m$ has a matching of size $s$. **Large matching degree conjecture.** For every $\varepsilon>0$,

$$
m_d^{s}(k,n)= \left(1-\left(1-\frac{s}{n}\right)^{k-d}+o(1)\right)\binom{n-d}{k-d}.
$$

This extends the perfect-matching threshold problem to smaller matchings. The paper presents it as a proposed generalization; the supplied text gives no resolution of the conjecture, although it records exact results in some small-uniformity cases.
record.source_name: Daniela Kühn, Deryk Osthus and Timothy Townsend, “Fractional and integer matchings in uniform hypergraphs”, arXiv:1304.6901 (2013).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1304.6901

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2013).

record.title: Infinite logconcavity conjecture for the sequence $\{d_{\ell}(m)\}$
record.statement:
Let $\{d_{\ell}(m)\}$ be the sequence described above, and define the operator

$$
\mathfrak{L}\left(\{x_k\}\right)=\left\{x_k^2-x_{k-1}x_{k+1}\right\}.
$$

A sequence is **infinitely logconcave** if $\mathfrak{L}^j(\{x_k\})$ is nonnegative for every $j\in\mathbb{N}$. **Infinite logconcavity conjecture.** The sequence $\{d_{\ell}(m)\}$ is infinitely logconcave.

Logconcavity of this sequence is known, including through ratio-monotonicity and the minimum conjecture, but infinite logconcavity is the stronger proposed property and is not resolved here.
record.source_name: Tewodros Amdeberhan, Atul Dixit, Xiao Guan, Lin Jiu and Victor H. Moll, “The unimodality of a polynomial coming from a rational integral. Back to the original proof”, arXiv:1304.7872 (2013).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1304.7872

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2013).

record.title: Arithmetic-progression conjecture for rank-generating functions
record.statement:
Let $F_{\lambda}(q)$ be the rank-generating function for partitions contained inside a partition $\lambda$, and let

$$
\lambda=\langle a,a-t,\dots,a-(b-1)t\rangle
$$

be a partition whose parts form an arithmetic progression. A polynomial is **unimodal** if its coefficients weakly increase and then weakly decrease. **Arithmetic-progression unimodality conjecture.** If $t\ge a/b$, then $F_{\lambda}(q)$ is unimodal. Equivalently, this asserts unimodality for all such arithmetic-progression partitions that begin with the smallest possible positive integer. The staircase case is known, but the conjecture remains open in general; the source also notes that some truncated staircases outside this range are nonunimodal.
record.source_name: Richard P. Stanley and Fabrizio Zanello, “Unimodality of partitions with distinct parts inside Ferrers shapes”, arXiv:1305.6083 (2015).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1305.6083

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2013).

record.title: Arbitrary-peak conjecture for rank-generating functions
record.statement: Let $F_{\lambda}(q)$ be the rank-generating function for partitions contained inside a partition $\lambda$. A polynomial is **unimodal** if its coefficients weakly increase and then weakly decrease; a peak is a local maximum in its coefficient sequence. **Arbitrary-peak conjecture.** For every integer $N\ge 2$, there exists a partition $\lambda$ such that $F_{\lambda}(q)$ is nonunimodal with (exactly?) $N$ peaks. The parenthetical qualification is part of the source statement, so it is unclear whether the intended assertion is exactly $N$ peaks or merely $N$ peaks; no resolution is supplied.
record.source_name: Richard P. Stanley and Fabrizio Zanello, “Unimodality of partitions with distinct parts inside Ferrers shapes”, arXiv:1305.6083 (2015).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1305.6083

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2013).

record.title: Edge-colouring conjecture for bipartite hypergraphs
record.statement:
A **bipartite $r$-uniform hypergraph with special side $S$** is one in which every edge meets $S$ in exactly one vertex. Assume

$$
\deg(u)\ge (r-1)\deg(v)
$$

for every $u\in S$ and $v\in V\setminus S$. **Edge-colouring conjecture.** If $H$ satisfies these conditions, then

$$
\chi'(H)=\Delta(H).
$$

Here $\chi'(H)$ is the edge-chromatic number and $\Delta(H)$ the maximum degree. The source says this would strengthen the preceding matching theorem, notes that it is proved when $|S|=2$, and records a stronger sufficient degree condition under which it holds.
record.source_name: Ron Aharoni, Pierre Charbit and David Howard, “On a Generalization of the Ryser-Brualdi-Stein Conjecture”, arXiv:1305.6164 (2013).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1305.6164

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of May 2013). “For even $n$ this is false, and Brualdi and Stein raised independently the following natural conjecture: In a Latin square of order $n$ there exists a partial transversal of size $n-1$.”

record.title: Average first negative value conjecture for Rankin–Selberg Fourier coefficients
record.statement:
Let $D_1$ and $D_2$ range over fundamental discriminants with $|D_1D_2|\leq x$, and let $p_1<p_2<\cdots$ be the primes. Define $\eta(D_1,D_2)$ to be the smallest $p_i$ such that

$$
\operatorname{sgn}(\sigma_{\chi_1,\chi_2}^{k-1}(p_i))=-1.
$$

**Average first negative value conjecture.** As $x\to\infty$, one expects

$$
\frac{\sum_{|D_1D_2|\leq x}\eta(D_1,D_2)}{\sum_{|D_1D_2|\leq x}1}\longrightarrow\theta,
$$

where

$$
\theta:=\sum_{\ell=1}^{\infty}\frac{p_\ell^2(p_\ell+2)}{2(p_\ell+1)^2}\prod_{i=1}^{\ell-1}\frac{2+p_i(p_i+2)}{2(p_i+1)^2}.
$$

The conjecture predicts that the average first prime at which the relevant Fourier coefficient has negative sign converges to the numerical constant $\theta=3.9750223902667539847734759105175510246019355513991\ldots$.
record.source_name: Benjamin Linowitz and Lola Thompson, “The sign changes of Fourier coefficients of Eisenstein series”, arXiv:1305.6356 (2013).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1305.6356

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2013).

record.title: Large-rank conjecture for rank-$k$ flats in matroids with no uniform minor
record.statement:
Let $\ell\ge 2$ be an integer, let $M$ be a rank-$r$ matroid, and let $U_{2,\ell+2}$ denote the rank-$2$ uniform matroid on $\ell+2$ elements. Let $q$ be the largest prime power such that $q\le \ell$. **Large-rank conjecture.** If $r$ is sufficiently large and $M$ has no $U_{2,\ell+2}$-minor, then, for every integer $k\ge 0$,

$$
W_k(M)\le \left[ {r} \atop {k}\right]_{q}.
$$

This strengthens the paper's main theorem by removing the requirement that the rank be large compared with $k$. The conjecture is presented as open; the preceding discussion indicates that the rank-$3$ obstruction is believed to be sporadic.
record.source_name: Peter Nelson, “The number of rank-k flats in a matroid with no U_2,n-minor”, arXiv:1306.0531 (2013).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1306.0531

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2013).

record.title: Conjecture on the extremal divisor count for almost all parameter pairs
record.statement:
For positive integers $k$ and $n$, let $d(k,n)$ denote the extremal divisor-count function studied in the paper: the minimum number of $k$-element subsets that can occur as divisors in an $n$-element set of positive integers.

**Divisor-count conjecture.** For most values of $k$ and $n$, specifically for all but finitely many values of $k$ and $n$,

$$
d(k,n)=\binom{n-1}{k}.
$$

The source notes that determining $d(k,n)$ for $n\neq 2k$ is open because the complementary subsets need not have the same cardinality; the conjecture predicts the displayed value except for finitely many parameter pairs.
record.source_name: Tony Huynh, “Extremal Problems for Subset Divisors”, arXiv:1306.0943 (2014).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1306.0943

Status: **open** according to the source (as of June 2013). “We end by mentioning that determining $d(k,n)$ for $n \neq 2k$ is also an open problem.”

record.title: Nowakowski's independent domination conjecture for categorical graph products
record.statement:
Let $G$ and $H$ be graphs, and let $i(G)$ denote the smallest cardinality of an independent dominating set in $G$, equivalently the cardinality of a smallest maximal independent set. **Nowakowski's conjecture.** For all graphs $G$ and $H$,

$$
i(G\times H)\geq i(G)\cdot i(H).
$$

This conjecture asks whether the independent domination number is supermultiplicative under the categorical product. It is cited in the source as an existing conjecture, and no resolution status is supplied.

record.title: Hyatt's unimodality conjecture for the type B polynomial $T_k(x)$
record.statement:
Let

$$
T_k(x)=\sum_{l=0}^{k}B_{k-l}(x^{k+1})(x^{k+1}-1)^l\sum_{i=l}^{k}{i\choose l}x^{-i},
$$

where $B_m(x)$ is the type $B$ Eulerian polynomial. **Hyatt's unimodality conjecture.** The polynomial $T_k(x)$ is unimodal for every integer $k\geq 0$. This conjecture concerns the coefficient sequence of the polynomial arising in the enumeration of signed permutations with bounded maximum drop size. The supplied text gives no evidence of a resolution.

record.title: Extremal real-part zeros attained by fibred stable alternating knots
record.statement:
For $n\geq1$, let $\Gamma_{2n}$ be the set of Alexander polynomials of alternating knots of genus $n$, and let $\delta_{2n}$ be the maximum of the maximal real part of a zero among polynomials in $\Gamma_{2n}$. **Extremal-attainment conjecture.** The quantity $\delta_{2n}$ exists for every $n\geq1$, and there is a fibred stable alternating knot $K_n$ such that

$$
\delta_{2n}(K_n)=\delta_{2n}.
$$

This combines existence of the extremal value with the assertion that it is realized by a fibred stable alternating knot.
record.source_name: Mikami Hirasawa and Kunio Murasugi, “Various stabilities of the Alexander polynomials of knots and links”, arXiv:1307.1578 (2013).

record.title: Jackson–Sokal maxmaxflow bound conjecture for chromatic roots
record.statement:
For a loopless graph $G$, let $\lambda_G(x,y)$ be the maximum number of edge-disjoint paths between distinct vertices $x$ and $y$, and let the **maxmaxflow** be

$$
\Lambda(G)=\max_{x\ne y}\lambda_G(x,y).
$$

A chromatic root is a zero of the chromatic polynomial. **Jackson–Sokal's conjecture.** For every value $\Lambda$, there exists a universal constant $C(\Lambda)<\infty$ such that all chromatic roots, real or complex, of all loopless graphs of maxmaxflow $\Lambda$ lie in

$$
|q|\le C(\Lambda).
$$

Moreover, $C(\Lambda)$ is conjectured to be linear in $\Lambda$. This would extend bounds in terms of the second-largest vertex degree to a matroidally meaningful graph parameter; the supplied text gives no resolution.
record.source_name: Gordon F. Royle and Alan D. Sokal, “Linear bound in terms of maxmaxflow for the chromatic roots of series-parallel graphs”, arXiv:1307.1721 (2013).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1307.1721

record.title: Erdős–Faudree–Gould–Scheinerman conjecture on cycles in sparse graphs
record.statement:
Let $G(n)$ be the family of graphs with $n$ vertices, $2n-2$ edges, and no proper subgraph of minimum degree $3$.

**Erdős–Faudree–Gould–Scheinerman conjecture.** Every $G\in G(n)$ contains cycles of length $i$ for every integer $3\le i\le k$, where $k$ tends to infinity with $n$.

The conjecture concerns how long an initial sequence of cycle lengths must occur in graphs just below the edge threshold forcing a proper subgraph of minimum degree $3$. The source gives no resolution.
record.source_name: András Gyárfás, “Problems and memories”, arXiv:1307.1768 (2013).

record.title: Information retention conjecture for bounded-degree majority dynamics
record.statement:
Let ${G_n}_{n in mathbb N}$ be a sequence of finite graphs with degrees bounded by $d$ and such that

$$
\lim_{n\to\infty}|V_n|=\infty.
$$

Here, $\delta(G_n,p)$ denotes the minimum probability of error when reconstructing the initial common opinion from the limiting opinions, and $p$ is the probability that an initial opinion agrees with the underlying signal, with $\frac12<p<1$.

**Information retention conjecture.** For every such sequence and every $\frac12<p<1$,

$$
\lim_{n\to\infty}\delta(G_n,p)=0.
$$

This conjecture asserts that bounded-degree majority dynamics retains enough information about the initial signal to permit asymptotically error-free reconstruction on every sequence of growing finite graphs. The source provides no resolution, so the conjecture is recorded as open.
record.source_name: Omer Tamuz and Ran J. Tessler, “Majority Dynamics and the Retention of Information”, arXiv:1307.4035 (2014).

record.title: Full-clique tiling conjecture for standard multigraphs
record.statement:
Let $M$ be a standard multigraph on $sk$ vertices. The **full $s$-clique** associated with an acyclic standard multigraph on $s$ vertices is its complement in the complete standard multigraph. Here $\delta(M)$ denotes the minimum degree. **Full-clique tiling conjecture.** For every $s,k\in\mathbb{N}$, if

$$
\delta(M)\geq 2(s-1)k-1,
$$

then $M$ contains $k$ disjoint full $s$-cliques.

This is presented as the complementary form of the equitable acyclic coloring conjecture. The supplied text gives no evidence that it has been resolved.
record.source_name: Andrzej Czygrinow, Louis DeBiasio, H. A. Kierstead and Theodore Molla, “An extension of the Hajnal-Szemeredi theorem to directed graphs”, arXiv:1307.4803 (2013).

record.title: Universal-clique tiling conjecture for standard multigraphs
record.statement:
Let $M$ be a standard multigraph on $sk$ vertices. An **universal $s$-clique** is an $s$-vertex clique whose every orientation contains every tournament on $s$ vertices. Let $\delta(M)$ denote the minimum degree. **Universal-clique tiling conjecture.** For every $s\geq 4$ and $k\in\mathbb{N}$, if

$$
\delta(M)\geq 2(s-1)k-1,
$$

then $M$ can be tiled with $k$ disjoint universal $s$-cliques.

The source says that subsequent theorems support this conjecture, but does not claim a proof. It combines with the forest embedding conjecture and other results to imply a directed graph factor statement.
record.source_name: Andrzej Czygrinow, Louis DeBiasio, H. A. Kierstead and Theodore Molla, “An extension of the Hajnal-Szemeredi theorem to directed graphs”, arXiv:1307.4803 (2013).

record.title: The type-$n$ dual-pair conjecture for umbral modules
record.statement:
Let $X$ be a Niemeier root system with Coxeter number $m$, and let $D$ be a discriminant of $H^X$. **Dual-pair conjecture.** If

$$
D=-n\lambda^2
$$

for some integer $\lambda$, then the representation $K^X_{r,-D/4m}$ has at least one dual pair of irreducible representations of type $n$ among its irreducible constituents. The conjecture extends the observed smallest-discriminant phenomenon; it was verified in the source for $X=A_1^{24}$, while the general statement remains open.
record.source_name: Miranda C. N. Cheng, John F. R. Duncan and Jeffrey A. Harvey, “Umbral Moonshine and the Niemeier Lattices”, arXiv:1307.5793 (2014).

record.title: Caporaso's Brill–Noether generality conjecture for maximally symmetric trivalent graphs
record.statement:
Let $g\geq 2$. A **trivalent graph of genus $g$ with largest possible automorphism group** means a trivalent graph whose automorphism group has maximal size among trivalent graphs of genus $g$. A graph is **Brill–Noether general** if, for every pair of positive integers $r$ and $d$ such that

$$
\rho^r_d(g)=g-(r+1)(g-d+r)
$$

is negative, it has no effective divisor of degree $d$ and rank at least $r$. **Caporaso's conjecture.** Every trivalent graph of genus $g\geq 2$ with largest possible automorphism group is Brill–Noether general. The paper disproves this conjecture by constructing Brill–Noether special maximally symmetric trivalent graphs in sufficiently large genus; the abstract states such counterexamples occur in every sufficiently large genus.
record.source_name: Timothy Leake and Dhruv Ranganathan, “Brill-Noether Theory of Maximally Symmetric Graphs”, arXiv:1307.7652 (2014).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1307.7652

record.title: Exponential localization conjecture for pointwise sampling functions on the Sierpinski gasket
record.statement:
Let $\beta_m$ be the level-$m$ vertex set of the Sierpinski gasket, let $y$ be a non-boundary vertex in $\beta_m$, and let $\phi_y^{(m)}$ be the pointwise sampling function satisfying $\phi_y^{(m)}(x)=\delta_{yx}$ for $x\in\beta_m$. For $x\in SG$, let $d_m(x,y)$ be the smallest number of level-$m$ cells separating $x$ and $y$. **Exponential localization conjecture.** There exist constants $c$ and $\alpha<1$, with $\alpha$ numerically about $1/3$, such that

$$
\left|\phi_y^{(m)}(x)\right|\le c\alpha^{d_m(x,y)}
$$

for all non-boundary vertices $y$ in $\beta_m$, all $x\in SG$, and all $m$. This conjecture, attributed in the source to earlier work on pointwise sampling functions, describes the rapid spatial decay observed numerically for both pointwise and cell sampling functions.
record.source_name: Robert J. Ravier and Robert S. Strichartz, “Sampling Theory with Average Values on the Sierpinski Gasket”, arXiv:1308.0079 (2015).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1308.0079

record.title: The average-size conjecture for coprime core partitions
record.statement:
Let $a,b\in\mathbb{N}$ be coprime. An $(a,b)$-core is a partition with no hook length divisible by $a$ or $b$; a self-conjugate $(a,b)$-core is one equal to its conjugate. The average size is taken over the finite sets of the relevant cores. **Average-size conjecture.** The average size of an $(a,b)$-core and the average size of a self-conjugate $(a,b)$-core are both equal to

$$
\frac{(a+b+1)(a-1)(b-1)}{24}.
$$

Equivalently, since the unique largest $(a,b)$-core is self-conjugate and has size $\frac{(a^2-1)(b^2-1)}{24}$, the average ratio between an $(a,b)$-core and the largest $(a,b)$-core is $\frac{a+b+1}{(a+1)(b+1)}$. Olsson and Stanton proved the asserted uniqueness and maximum-size formula, while the average-size assertion is presented as a conjecture.
record.source_name: Drew Armstrong, Christopher R. H. Hanusa and Brant C. Jones, “Results and conjectures on simultaneous core partitions”, arXiv:1308.0572 (2014).

record.title: Wang and Lih's planar graph square-coloring conjecture
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a planar graph, let $g(G)$ denote its girth, let $\operatorname{\Delta(G)}$ denote its maximum degree, and let $\chi^2(G)$ denote the chromatic number of its square. **Wang and Lih's conjecture.** For any integer $k \geq 5$, there exists an integer $M(k)$ such that for every planar graph $G$ satisfying $g(G) \geq k$ and $\operatorname{\Delta(G)} \geq M(k)$, 

$$
\chi^2(G)=\operatorname{\Delta(G)}+1.
$$

The claim asks when the general lower bound $\chi^2(G)\geq \operatorname{\Delta(G)}+1$ is attained for sufficiently sparse planar graphs. The paper strengthens the known results on square-coloring sparse graphs, but the stated conjecture is not resolved in the supplied text.
record.source_name: Marthe Bonamy, Benjamin Lévêque and Alexandre Pinlou, “List coloring the square of sparse graphs with large degree”, arXiv:1308.4197 (2013).

record.title: Interval-completion bound for the defining ideal of a numerical semigroup tangent cone
record.statement:
Let $H=\langle a_1,\dots,a_r\rangle$ be a numerical semigroup, and let $\widetilde H$ be its interval completion, the numerical semigroup generated by all integers in the interval $[a_1,a_r]$. Let $I_H^*$ and $I_{\widetilde H}^*$ denote the defining ideals of the tangent cones of $H$ and $\widetilde H$, respectively. **Interval-completion bound conjecture.** For every numerical semigroup $H$,

$$
\mu(I_H^*)\leq\mu(I_{\widetilde H}^*).
$$

The conjecture compares the number of minimal generators of the tangent-cone defining ideal with that of the interval completion, whose generators fill the interval between the smallest and largest generators of $H$. The source gives no proof or evidence of resolution, so the status remains open.
record.source_name: Jürgen Herzog and Dumitru I. Stamate, “On the defining equations of the tangent cone of a numerical semigroup ring”, arXiv:1308.4644 (2014).

record.title: The extremal-frequency form of Frankl's conjecture
record.statement:
For a union-closed family $mathcal A$, define its maximum element frequency by

$$
\phi(\mathcal A)=\max_{u\in U(\mathcal A)}|\mathcal A_u|.
$$

Let $mathcal\foon(n)$ be the minimum of $mathcal\foon(\mathcal A)$ over all union-closed families with $n\geq2$ member-sets.

**Frankl's extremal-frequency conjecture.** For every integer $n\geq2$,

$$
\phi(n)\geq \tfrac{n}{2}.
$$

The paper explicitly calls this a trivial reformulation of the union-closed sets conjecture. No resolution is stated.
record.source_name: Henning Bruhn and Oliver Schaudt, “The journey of the union-closed sets conjecture”, arXiv:1309.3297 (2013).
record.references:

record.title: High-entropy winning-shift conjecture
record.statement:
Fix a finite alphabet $S$. For a subshift $X\subset S^\mathbb{X}$, let $h(X)$ denote its topological entropy and let $W(X)$ denote its winning shift. **High-entropy winning-shift conjecture.** For every $\epsilon>0$ there exists $\delta>0$ such that, if

$$
h(X)>\log_2|S|-\delta,
$$

then

$$
h(W(X))>1-\epsilon.
$$

This predicts that subshifts with entropy arbitrarily close to the maximum possible entropy have winning shifts with entropy arbitrarily close to $1$.
record.source_name: Ville Salo and Ilkka Törmä, “Playing with Subshifts”, arXiv:1310.0650 (2013).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1310.0650

record.title: Gromov's filling area conjecture for all genera
record.statement: Let a membrane have genus $p\ge 0$ and a prescribed boundary metric, and let an **Ahlfors map** mean the extremal conformal map used to compute its area through isothermic coordinates. **Gromov's filling area conjecture.** The filling area conjecture is true for all genus $p\ge 0$, and its proof will employ an Ahlfors map as one of the ingredients. The conjecture is stated as still open in the source; the genus-zero case follows from Pu's theorem under Loewner's work, while higher-genus cases remain unresolved.

record.title: Bubboloni–Praeger–Spiga conjecture for the normal covering number of alternating groups
record.statement:
Let $n=p_1^{\alpha_1}\cdots p_r^{\alpha_r}$, where $r\geq2$, the $p_i$ are primes, $\alpha_i\in\mathbb{N}$, and $p_i<p_j$ for $i<j$. Define

$$
g(n):=\frac{n}{2}\left(1-\frac{1}{p_1}\right)\left(1-\frac{1}{p_2}\right)+2.
$$

Assume that $n$ is even, $r\geq2$, and $n\neq2p_2,12$.

**Normal covering conjecture for $A_n$.**

$$
\gamma(A_n)=g(n).
$$

This is the alternating-group counterpart of the proposed formula for $\gamma(S_n)$. The paper establishes linear growth and discusses evidence for the formula, but the exact value remains open in the stated generality.
record.source_name: Daniela Bubboloni, Cheryl E. Praeger and Pablo Spiga, “Conjectures on the normal covering number of the finite symmetric and alternating groups”, arXiv:1310.2911 (2013).

record.title: Conjectured recursion for the ML degree of Grassmannians
record.statement:
For $n\geq4$, let $\operatorname{Gr}_{2,n}\subseteq\mathbb{P}^{\binom{n}{2}-1}$ denote the Grassmannian of lines in $\mathbb{P}^{n-1}$, with homogeneous coordinates $p_{ij}$, and let $\operatorname{MLdegree}(X)$ denote the maximum likelihood degree of a variety $X$. **Grassmannian ML-degree recursion.** For $n\geq4$,

$$
\operatorname{MLdegree}(\operatorname{Gr}_{2,n})=\operatorname{MLdegree}(\operatorname{Gr}_{2,n+1}\cap\{p_{12}=0\}).
$$

The conjecture is proposed to motivate a recursive formula for ML degrees of Grassmannians. The source reports computational data for $n=4,5,6$ but gives no proof or resolution.

record.title: The proposed formula for the maximum number of directed 2-factors in odd tournaments
record.statement:
Let $\rho(n,n)$ denote the maximum number of directed $2$-factors among tournaments on $n$ vertices. Let $D_p$ be the number of derangements of ${1,\ldots,p}$.

**Odd-tournament maximum conjecture.** For every odd positive integer $n>7$,

$$
\rho(n,n)=\frac{n+1}{2}D_{\frac{n+1}{2}}\left(\frac{n-1}{2}\right)!^3.
$$

The formula is motivated by the lower and upper bounds established in the paper and by computational evidence for small odd values. Determining the exact maximum for all odd $n>7$ remains open.

record.title: The complete-bipartite majority out-domination conjecture
record.statement:
Let $K_{r,s}$ be a complete bipartite graph with $2\leq r\leq s$, and let $DOM^+_{maj}(K_{r,s})$ denote the minimum cardinality of a set that is a majority out-dominating set in an orientation of $K_{r,s}$, as defined in the source.

**Complete-bipartite majority out-domination conjecture.**

$$
DOM^+_{maj}(K_{r,s})=\begin{cases}2&\text{if }r+s\text{ is even},\\\\3&\text{if }r+s\text{ is odd}.
\end{cases}
$$

The conjecture follows a proposition establishing the corresponding signed-function value $dom^+_{maj}(K_{r,s})=4-(r+s)$ for every orientation. The stronger cardinality assertion for $DOM^+_{maj}$ is stated here without a resolution.

record.title: Interior optimal-barrier conjecture for the square
record.statement:
Let a **barrier** for the unit square be a curve whose removal blocks every line intersecting the square, and call a barrier **optimal** if it has minimum length among all barriers. A barrier is **interior** if it lies inside the unit square.

**Interior optimal-barrier conjecture.** An optimal barrier for the square is interior.

If true, the paper's lower bound for interior barriers would give a nontrivial lower bound for arbitrary barriers of the unit square. The claim is presented as open; the paper has such a lower bound only under a locality condition, in particular for interior barriers.

record.title: The universal dynamics monoid conjecture for finite directed acyclic graphs
record.statement:
Let $\Gamma$ be a finite directed acyclic graph. Its **universal dynamics monoid** $D(\Gamma)$ is the smallest quotient of $\operatorname{\mathbf{HK}}_\Gamma$ through which all evaluation maps from update systems supported on $\Gamma$ factor. **Universal dynamics monoid conjecture.**

$$
D(\Gamma) \simeq \operatorname{\mathbf{HK}}_\Gamma
$$

The conjecture extends the proved equality $D(\Gamma_n) \simeq \operatorname{\mathbf{HK}}_{\Gamma_n}=\mathrm{K}_n$ from the family of graphs $\Gamma_n$ to every finite directed acyclic graph. It had been computationally checked for all instances with at most four vertices and for most graphs on five vertices; a general conceptual proof remains open.
